title: Anthropic IPO: Why Wall Street is betting big on Claude AI maker - ​Anthropic IPO could value AI firm at up to $1.6 trillion | The Economic Times
text:
Anthropic is preparing for one of the biggest stock market debuts in history, with the maker of Claude AI expected to command a valuation of around $1.4 trillion or higher. The company initially indicated an IPO price range of $70-$78 per share, implying a valuation of approximately $1.33 trillion. However, strong investor demand has prompted discussions about pricing the shares above the initial range, potentially pushing its valuation towards $1.5 trillion-$1.6 trillion. The shares are expected to list on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. (Sources: Yahoo Finance, The Guardian)

Amazon and Google are set to hold more than 28% of Anthropic's outstanding shares following its IPO and concurrent private placement, highlighting the growing financial ties between the AI developer and its cloud partners. According to regulatory disclosures, Amazon is expected to own nearly 15% of the company, while Google's stake will be around 14%. Both companies are also major investors, cloud infrastructure providers and commercial partners for Anthropic, creating closely interconnected business relationships.

Anthropic's public listing is expected to generate substantial gains for a diverse group of existing investors, including venture capital firms, major technology companies and sovereign wealth funds. According to The Wall Street Journal, the company was most recently valued at $965 billion in private markets, setting the stage for a potentially significant valuation increase through its IPO. Early backers stand to benefit from the jump in valuation as Anthropic transitions into a publicly traded company.

New Street Research has initiated coverage of Anthropic with a Buy rating and a $105 price target ahead of its stock market debut. The target implies approximately 42% upside from the midpoint of the proposed $70-$78 IPO price range. The brokerage expects Anthropic's annual revenue to surge to $505 billion by 2030 from an estimated $53 billion in 2026, driven by accelerating artificial intelligence adoption and demand for computing capacity. It also expects the company's computing capacity to expand six-fold to 30 gigawatts by the end of the decade.

Despite strong investor interest, Anthropic's IPO comes with significant risks. The Guardian highlighted concerns around the company's governance structure, capital-intensive operations and its ability to translate growing demand for Claude into sustainable profits. Anthropic's prospectus also indicates that public shareholders will collectively hold only 49.9% of the company's voting power, limiting their ability to influence corporate decisions. Analysts caution that heavy IPO demand could support an initial price surge but does not guarantee lasting gains, particularly amid volatility in technology stocks.
